diagnosis.root_cause: The router has not checked in for 7.4 hours, exceeding the danger threshold of 4 hours. The ONU, optical levels, OLT, VLAN, RADIUS state, and sessions are healthy, so the stale heartbeat is isolated to the router management/reachability path.
evidence: The router heartbeat is 7.4 hours stale, which is in the danger range above 4 hours.
The ONU is online and responding, with RX -20.61 dBm and TX 2.40 dBm, both within normal EPON ranges.
Seven-day optical telemetry is stable: RX variation is within the healthy noise range, TX is stable, distance remains 152, and TX bias remains healthy without a rising trend.
All tested peers on EPON0/2 are online, so there is no ONU, splitter, or PON-port outage.
The OLT answers ping and SNMP and has normal CPU, memory, and temperature, ruling out an OLT failure.
The customer VLAN is correctly provisioned as VLAN 1062.
RADIUS exists, matches CRM line ID, and the customer has a normal long-lived session; there is no missing entry, suspension, line-ID conflict, replication issue, or session flapping.
The fault is therefore the stale/unreachable router heartbeat rather than an EPON or authentication fault.

remediation.action: Verify router power and local connectivity, then test reachability to TK_AZ_Bitola_Jadranska01 and its management services. Inspect WAN/uplink, management interface, logs, and any firewall or monitoring-agent failure; restore or restart the router/agent if required and confirm a fresh heartbeat.

ground_truth.root_cause: The BNG TK_AZ_Bitola_Jadranska01 stopped checking in 7.4 hours ago. Customers behind it lost their sessions at the same moment. The optical plant is entirely unaffected: ONUs remain registered and are returning normal signal readings.
expected_reasoning: Router heartbeat is 7.4 hours stale, past the 4 hour danger threshold
The ONU is online with RX -20.6 and TX 2.4, both normal, and the live probe confirms it
Every peer on the port is also online with normal optical readings
OLT ping, SNMP and device metrics are all healthy
So the optical layer is working and the fault is not in the fibre plant
Sessions across customers on this router ended together 7.4 hours ago
Throughput fell to zero at the same moment while the ONUs stayed registered
Healthy ONUs with dead sessions is the router signature: the optical layer carries no traffic without the BNG
The blast radius follows the router, not the OLT, so every customer it serves is affected
distractors: ONU status is online everywhere, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The OLT health check reports healthy, which is correct but irrelevant
Optical readings are perfect, which points away from where the fault is
